A **new user send** and an **internal retry** can reuse the same document row. The distinction is the entry path, not whether a row is newly inserted.

- **New user send:** `TaxAutomations::ExportAsync` authorizes and validates the request, selects accepted documents, finds or creates their send records, and dispatches to Instead. Instead then enqueues a new export workflow. A repeat user send can reuse an existing record. See [ExportAsync](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:53) and [record reuse](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:212).
- **Workflow rerun:** uses the document IDs already stored in the workflow arguments. After finding, linking, or creating the Instead entity, it loads those rows and calls `PrepareForSend` before starting uploads. See [workflow preparation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/export_async_workflow.rb:22).

The preparation/reset path is:

1. `PrepareForSend` authorizes export and opens a transaction.
2. For each named row, it calls `resend!` when allowed, then `reset!` when allowed.
3. After commit, it broadcasts each row’s status and returns the same rows for upload. See [PrepareForSend](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/prepare_for_send.rb:27).

The state machines make a failed upload retryable: `resend!` moves eligible processing states—including `error` and `exceeded`—to `sent`; `reset!` moves `uploading`, `uploaded`, or `failed` to `waiting`. These transitions clear `failure_reason`. **Reset does not clear `uploaded_at` or delete the Instead-specific document row.** See [document transitions](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/document.rb:39).

There is also a narrower **byte-transfer worker retry**. It does not run this preparation/reset path: it calls `upload!` only when allowed, so a row already left `uploading` stays there, then retries using the buffered upload target. A missing target raises `TargetExpiredError`; its buffer lifetime follows the signature expiry, with a one-day fallback for undated targets. See [transfer retry](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/documents/transfer_bytes_to_presigned_target.rb:27) and [target lifetime](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/upload_target_buffer.rb:13).
